messages:
alex: CI is failing across multiple pipelines for the last ~30m, looks like the test DB mock is returning ECONNREFUSED on startup. https://ci.redwood-internal/pipelines/3421/jobs

maria: seeing the same. failing jobs: integration-tests, e2e-kafka, nightly-regressions. lots of `psql: could not connect to server: Connection refused` in the logs. :confused:

jamie: @alex can you paste the failing job link? I want to check docker compose logs.

alex: https://ci.redwood-internal/jobs/3421-5678/logs - grep output: `docker-entrypoint.sh: running /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/*` then `could not bind socket: Address already in use` repeatedly.

ci-bot: [ci] job integration-tests #257 failed: exit code 1 — retry with rebuild? :warning:

maria: repro steps locally: `./dev/infra up db-mock` -> sometimes it dies after 5s with the same bind error. Might be port collision on the CI host when multiple runners spawn.

ben: I just hit it when running the nightly job manually. Host-level process `postgres` was already running from previous container and not cleaned up, so container couldn't bind to 5432. We have a race in our runner cleanup.

jamie: ok this smells like the runner image change from last night that introduced systemd shim -> changed process PID behavior. @sre-bot any recent runner config rollouts?

sre-bot: config-rollout v1.14 deployed 1744999000 to staging, 1745000100 to prod. Change: `docker-run --init` -> `--init --privileged` (attempt to fix nested container permissions).

alex: that might explain it. the privileged flag may change how processes are reaped. Could leave stray postgres on the host.

maria: quick mitigation: can someone rerun failing pipelines but set `SKIP_DB_MOCK=true` for tests that can use the real ephemeral DB instead? If not, we can temporarily pin runner to previous config.

jamie: I'll kick off a targeted rerun with `SKIP_DB_MOCK` for integration-tests and e2e that don't strictly require the mock. Manual reruns: https://ci.redwood-internal/pipelines/3421/retry

ben: started a rerun for nightly-regressions with SKIP_DB_MOCK. queue position looks good.

alex: also requesting a short bisect: @maria can you run `git bisect` between the last known-good commit and HEAD for infra/ci-runner? If it's config-only, we can rollback quickly.

maria: starting bisect now. locally reproduces when runner uses the new flags. will report commit if found.

ci-bot: [alert] 3 more jobs failed in the last 10m: integration-tests x2, e2e-kafka x1.

jamie: temporary hotfix: pinned runner to v1.13 on the prod worker group. rolling out now. I'll monitor job queue and host process list.

ben: confirmed: after pinning, new jobs spin up cleanly and containers bind to 5432 fine. Old stuck postgres processes remain on some hosts, cleaning them up now with `pkill -f postgres` on the affected nodes.

alex: nice. action items: 1) revert the privileged flag rollout until we fix runner cleanup (jamie) 2) add a CI healthcheck that kills leftover host postgres before starting containers (maria) 3) add an infra test that simulates rapid runner churn (ben) 4) postmortem if we don't have one in 24h (alex).

maria: bisect result: commit 9f3b2c1 in infra/runner-config introduced `--privileged` wrapper. Reverting that fixes the local repro.

jamie: I've created rollback PR #1982 to pin config and rollback the flag. Deploying to prod worker group now.

alex: thanks all. for follow-up, please add a GH issue with steps to reproduce + the commands we used to cleanup. Also add a test that runs `./dev/infra up db-mock` in a rapid-concurrency loop.

ben: created issue infra#443 with logs and mitigation steps. tagging @oncall for next 24h monitoring. :eyes:

jamie: closing the immediate incident — CI green for the reruns. Leaving this thread open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
